doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

chapter: Synths, the section and stopping playing
title: Horn players and synthesizers
summary: Hey says synths are fine as their own instrument but hard to substitute for trumpet; he has added real trumpet to synth parts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Do horn players still hate synthesizers?

If, you know if they’re abusing a synth, yeah of course. If they’re you know taking the place of horn parts, which still is kind of difficult to do for trumpet. You can kind of get away with it on baritone saxophone and, you know, if you’re going to have orchestra trombone pads you can kind of get away with that and French horns you can sort of get away with it. But you know synth is, if you use it like another musical instrument, you know, playing stuff that should be played by a synthesizer, then fine.
Did you ever have a situation where you were adding a real trumpet to synthesizer trumpets to give it a little authenticity?
Yeah. But if they were — if I was called they would probably have me writing a horn chart and playing with a section rather than do that. I have done a few of those playing
along, not necessarily playing along with synth trumpets but adding a trumpet to a synth part.
